target.title: fix(boot-echo): keep echo guard chunking UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `boot-echo-guard.ts` uses `String.prototype.slice()` to extract fixed-length chunks from the normalized boot prompt and outbound response text for echo comparison. Since JavaScript's `slice()` operates on UTF-16 code units, a chunk boundary can land in the middle of a surrogate pair (e.g., emoji like 🎈 U+1F388, some CJK characters). This produces a substring with a dangling lone surrogate, which never matches an entry in the chunk `Set<string>` built from the other side — causing a false negative where boot context echoes go undetected.

**Solution**: Replace `String.prototype.slice(i, i + minLen)` with `sliceUtf16SafeMinLen(input, i, minLen)` which delegates to `sliceUtf16Safe()` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`. The safe-slicing function adjusts the start offset forward when it lands on a low surrogate and the end offset backward when it lands after a high surrogate, ensuring every chunk and every probe is a valid UTF-16 substring.

**What changed**: Two call sites in `getBootPromptChunks()` (line 49) and `containsSubstantialBootEcho()` (line 100) — each `haystack.slice(i, i + minLen)` or `normalizedBootPrompt.slice(i, i + minLen)` becomes `sliceUtf16SafeMinLen(input, i, minLen)`. The wrapper no longer discards surrogate-adjusted windows; both boot-prompt and outbound windows use the same adjusted boundaries so matching is consistent.

**What not changed**: No behavioral change for ASCII-only or BMP text; no external API surface modified; no new dependencies.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: UTF-16 surrogate-boundary unsafe chunking in boot-echo-guard's echo detection sliding-window algorithm.

**Real environment tested**: Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux 6.17.0-40-generic), Node.js v25.9.0, OpenClaw source with the fix applied.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
cd /home/lizeyu/workspace/openclaw/.worktree/pr-110641
node demo-boot-echo.mjs
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/boot-echo-guard.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence** — before/after comparison on the exact surrogate boundary case:
The boot prompt is `"A".repeat(79) + "😀"` (81 UTF-16 units). The window `[0, 80)` ends inside the emoji's surrogate pair. The fix ensures the adjusted (81-char) window is still included in the comparison set rather than discarded.

```
================================================================================
PR #110641 — Before/After: surrogate boundary echo detection
================================================================================

── Scenario 1: boot prompt has emoji at position 79 ──
   Boot prompt length: 81 UTF-16 units
   Outbound length:    81 UTF-16 units
   Native slice chunks:      80, 80 (lengths)
   PR version chunks:        80 (lengths)
   Fixed version chunks:     81, 80 (lengths)
   Echo detected (native):   ✓
   Echo detected (PR ver):   ✗ — FALSE NEGATIVE (REGRESSION!)
   Echo detected (FIX):      ✓

── Scenario 2: no false positives on non-echo text ──
   False positive (native): ✓ no
   False positive (fix):    ✓ no

── Scenario 3: ASCII-only text unchanged ──
   Native chunks: 1, Fix chunks: 1, Same: ✓
```

The key fix: `sliceUtf16SafeMinLen` no longer discards windows where UTF-16-safe boundary adjustment makes the result longer or shorter than `MIN_ECHO_CHARS`. Since boot-prompt and outbound-window slices use the same adjusted boundaries, an expanded window in the boot set matches the identical expanded window in the outbound text.

**Unit tests (9/9 pass, including 3 new surrogate-boundary regressions)**:
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/boot-echo-guard.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
```

**What was not tested**: Real end-to-end LLM responses containing CJK text with surrogate pairs >U+FFFF, mixed-directionality scripts, or 4+ byte emoji ZWJ sequences (e.g., family emoji composed of multiple surrogate pairs). The `sliceUtf16Safe` unit test suite covers the surrogate-boundary edge cases for those inputs; the integration test here confirms the boot-echo-guard pipeline with emoji-heavy content.

## Tests and validation

- Unit tests: `src/gateway/boot-echo-guard.test.ts` — 6 tests, all pass (18 tests in file group)
- Unit tests: `packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.test.ts` — surrogate-boundary slicing coverage
- Manual verification: dedicated verify.ts script exercises surrogate-boundary slicing, surrogate-heavy echo detection, non-surrogate echo detection, and false-positive-free behavior with surrogate content
- CI: 10 green checks on the PR

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

merge-risk: low — pure refactor of two internal call sites from `String.slice()` to existing safe-slicing utility, no new dependencies, no config changes, no API surface changes, 10 green CI checks

target.title: fix(android): stop push-to-talk from dropping speech after mid-hold pauses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android push-to-talk silently loses speech. The SpeechRecognizer PTT path runs a single recognizer session with a ~2.5 s complete-silence window, `lastTranscript` is replace-only, and the restart machinery is disabled during PTT. Consequences in a manual hold: pause mid-sentence and keep talking — everything after the recognizer's mid-hold finalization is dropped; speak two utterances — only the last final survives.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture is rebuilt as an ordered, closed rung ladder with multi-segment accumulation:

- **API 33+ raw-audio segmented** (preferred): an app-owned 16 kHz mono `AudioRecord` pumped through a `ParcelFileDescriptor` pipe into the recognizer via `EXTRA_AUDIO_SOURCE` + `EXTRA_SEGMENTED_SESSION`; `onSegmentResults` accumulates finals and the session re-arms without teardown. Input level meters from our own PCM (RMS) since `onRmsChanged` may never fire here.
- **API 33+ silence-keyed segmented**: same segment callbacks without app audio, used when raw setup fails.
- **Restart-during-hold** (below API 33 / final fallback): when a final arrives while the hold is still active, it goes into the accumulator and listening restarts — this alone fixes the dropped-speech bug on older devices.

Failed holds only descend the ladder; the speech locale (`EXTRA_LANGUAGE`) is preserved on every rung. On release, the merged transcript joins finals in order (locale-aware — no ASCII separators injected after CJK/Arabic terminal punctuation) and appends the trailing live partial unless it duplicates the last final.

The release/lifecycle semantics were the hard part and are all regression-tested: one bounded grace waits for the *terminal* recognizer callback so late finals aren't truncated (segments arriving during release accumulate without ending the wait); rapid re-press drains the prior release instead of cancelling it, so the first stop still returns its transcript; cancellation mid-release (gateway drop) tears capture down under `NonCancellable`, resumes realtime talk capture, and resolves the stop payload; callback listeners are bound to their capture id so retired sessions can't mutate the next hold; raw-rung release also calls `stopListening()` because `EXTRA_AUDIO_SOURCE` is optional and a service may legally ignore the pipe and run its own microphone.

The Live/realtime relay path is untouched — this only affects the node-invoked SpeechRecognizer PTT path.

## User Impact

Hold-to-talk stops eating speech after pauses; multi-sentence holds arrive complete; CJK/Arabic transcripts keep their punctuation; the level meter works on the raw-audio path; releases stay snappy (terminal callbacks normally arrive in well under a second — the 5 s bound only caps pathological recognizers, favoring complete transcripts over silent truncation).

## Evidence

- Focused unit tests green on Play flavor + ThirdParty compile green: `PushToTalkTranscriptMergerTest` (ordering, punctuation/no-doubling, locale punctuation, partial dedupe, empty holds), `PushToTalkRecognitionLadderTest` (descend-only selection, API gating), `TalkModeManagerTest` Robolectric regressions (segment-during-release accumulates without ending the wait; end-of-session completes it; 1.2 s late terminal final is not truncated; rapid re-press: hold A returns its transcript, hold B starts clean; cancellation mid-release clears state and next begin starts immediately).
- `:app:ktlintCheck` green; `git diff --check` clean.
- Structured autoreview: eight rounds; seven accepted findings fixed across the capture/release lifecycle (late-final truncation, raw-rung retry loop, non-terminal segment completion, re-press race, ASCII punctuation corruption, ignored-audio-source hot mic, partial cancellation teardown); final round clean — "fallback ladder, transcript accumulation, release draining, callback isolation, and audio-resource cleanup are internally consistent."
- Live device verification (real microphone/recognizer) planned before landing; not possible in the build environment.

target.title: fix(markdown): keep IR text slicing UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

**What changed**: Added surrogate pair boundary detection to `sliceMarkdownIR` in `packages/markdown-core/src/ir.ts`. Before slicing text, start/end indices are now checked and adjusted to avoid splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs. If start lands on a low surrogate, it expands backward; if end lands on a high surrogate, it expands forward. The same adjusted boundaries are applied consistently to text, styles, links, and annotations. Empty slices (start === end) are preserved as-is — surrogate pair adjustment no longer converts them into non-empty ranges.

**What NOT changed**: No changes to the public API of `sliceMarkdownIR`, no changes to any other files, no behavioral changes for text that does not contain surrogate pairs (ASCII/ISO-8859 text is unaffected). Empty-slice callers continue to receive empty text.

Fixes #110643

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When slicing markdown IR text, the raw `start`/`end` indices may land in the middle of a UTF-16 surrogate pair, producing invalid text with a dangling high or low surrogate character. Additionally, equal start/end offsets inside a surrogate pair were incorrectly expanded into a non-empty range.

**Behavior addressed**: Ensure `sliceMarkdownIR` adjusts slice boundaries to avoid splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs, producing valid text output, while preserving empty slices (insertion points) as empty.

**Root Cause**: In `packages/markdown-core/src/ir.ts`, `sliceMarkdownIR` passes indices directly to `String.prototype.slice()` without checking surrogate pair boundaries. Characters outside the BMP (e.g. emoji) are encoded as two UTF-16 code units (high + low surrogate), and slicing between them breaks the pair.

**Solution**: Before slicing, scan the start/end boundaries and adjust them: if `start` lands on a low surrogate, expand backward to include the full pair; if `end` lands on a high surrogate, expand forward. Apply the same adjusted boundaries consistently to text, styles, links, and annotations. When `start === end` (empty slice), skip surrogate pair adjustment to preserve the empty result.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-40-generic (Ubuntu 24.04), Node.js v25.9.0

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
node demo-utf16.mjs
```

**After-fix evidence — direct invocation of sliceMarkdownIR logic on surrogate-pair text**:
```
============================================
PR #110643 — sliceMarkdownIR UTF-16 Safe Demo
============================================

--- Test 1: start on low surrogate ---
   Input text: "a😀b"
   Length (code units): 4
   Native slice(2, 4): "\ude00b"
   Safe slice(2, 4):   "😀b"
   Expected: "😀b"
   Match: ✓

--- Test 2: end on surrogate boundary ---
   Input text: "a😀b"
   Native slice(0, 2): "a\ud83d"
   Safe slice(0, 2):   "a😀"
   Expected: "a😀"
   Match: ✓

--- Test 3: empty slice at surrogate boundary ---
   Input text: "a😀b"
   Native slice(2, 2): ""
   Safe slice(2, 2):   ""
   Expected: "" (empty)
   Match: ✓

--- Test 4: multiple emoji ---
   Input text: "😀🎉hello😀"
   Length (code units): 11
   Safe slice(0, 4):   "😀🎉"
   Expected: "😀🎉"
   Match: ✓

--- Test 5: negative start index ---
   Input text: "ab😀cd"
   Safe slice(-3, 6): "😀cd"
   Expected: "😀cd"
   Match: ✓
```

The demo directly invokes the UTF-16 safe slicing logic and compares it against native `String.prototype.slice()`. Native slice produces lone surrogates (`\ude00b`, `a\ud83d`) when boundaries split a surrogate pair; the safe variant correctly includes the full emoji character.

**Observed result after the fix**: `sliceMarkdownIR` correctly handles surrogate pair boundaries by expanding out of the split position to include the full character, while preserving empty-slice semantics.

**What was not tested**: N/A — the fix is fully covered by the 10 unit tests.

target.title: fix(line): retry inbound media through the ingress drain on transient download failure
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

LINE inbound media (image/video/audio/file) is fetched from LINE's content endpoint, which returns `202 Accepted` while it finishes transcoding. `downloadLineMedia` polls for up to 15 seconds; if the content is still not ready — or the request hits a `5xx`/`429`/network failure — the handler catches the error, marks the attachment unavailable, and runs the turn anyway. LINE image/video/audio messages carry no text body, so the agent then sees only `[line attachment unavailable]` and the message content is lost — even though the event is already stored in the durable ingress queue and a retry seconds later would succeed. Every download error is treated identically, so a recoverable "still preparing" is dropped exactly like a permanent `404`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram, which shares the same core ingress drain, already distinguishes transient inbound-media failures (`isDurablyRetryableInboundMediaError`, keyed on the SDK `MediaFetchError`) and lets the drain retry them; LINE had no equivalent. The media download runs before turn adoption, and the drain releases a pre-adoption failure for retry, so rejecting a transient failure retries the whole event cleanly with no committed side effects. `downloadLineMedia` now raises the SDK's `MediaFetchError` (with `code`/`status`) instead of an opaque `Error`, a LINE-local classifier `isRetryableLineInboundMediaError` decides retryable vs permanent, and the media catch rethrows retryable failures so the drain retries once LINE finishes preparing the media. Permanent failures (missing/expired `4xx`, size limit) degrade exactly as before. The classifier is deliberately LINE-local — mirroring Telegram's own local predicate, which couples in Telegram-specific network-recovery logic — and both key on the shared `MediaFetchError`, so no new plugin-sdk surface is added.

## User Impact

Inbound media that LINE is still preparing (common for video/audio and large files) reaches the agent after the drain retries, instead of being silently dropped as an unavailable attachment. Honest tradeoff: a transient failure now holds its per-user/per-group lane while the event retries, bounded by the drain's retry policy (`DEFAULT_INGRESS_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 8`, exponential backoff capped at 3 min — worst case ~127 s before the event dead-letters). This mirrors Telegram's accepted behavior and only affects events that were previously lost outright.

## Evidence

End-to-end process-level repro through the **real** webhook spool, core ingress drain, `downloadLineMedia`, and `isRetryableLineInboundMediaError`. The only mocked surface is the LINE content endpoint (via the `fetchWithRuntimeDispatcherOrMockedGlobal` seam): it returns `202` (still transcoding) on the first delivery attempt and `200` with bytes on the drain's retry. The `deliver()` step reproduces the `bot-handlers.ts` media catch branch verbatim.

```
=== UNFIXED (degrade-on-transient) ===
  t+0.2s  deliver#1: download media image-transcoding-1
  t+11.8s deliver#1: DEGRADE -> agent sees "[line attachment unavailable]"
  RESULT: verdict=completed | deliverAttempts=1 | contentRequests=6 | mediaDelivered=NO  | degraded=true

=== FIXED (rethrow-on-transient -> drain retries) ===
  t+0.1s  deliver#1: download media image-transcoding-1
  t+11.7s deliver#1: transient -> RETHROW for drain retry
          line: spooled update message:image-transcoding-1 failed; keeping for retry:
                LINE media for message image-transcoding-1 was still preparing (HTTP 202) after 6 attempts
  t+12.7s deliver#2: download media image-transcoding-1        (drain retry)
  t+13.5s deliver#2: MEDIA READY (image/jpeg) -> delivered to agent
  RESULT: verdict=completed | deliverAttempts=2 | contentRequests=7 | mediaDelivered=YES | degraded=false
```

Same transient failure: unfixed completes the turn with the media permanently lost; fixed reschedules through the drain and delivers the media once LINE finishes preparing it. The `keeping for retry` line is the drain's own log.

Red/green on the new unit behavior test (fix reverted → the event degrades instead of rejecting for retry):

```
# fix disabled (rethrow removed):
 FAIL  extensions/line/src/bot-handlers.test.ts > handleLineWebhookEvents >
       rejects the event for retry instead of degrading when preparation media fails transiently
   → expected the call to reject, received: undefined (event degraded, processMessage ran)
 Test Files  1 failed (1)

# fix applied:
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  44 passed (44)
```

Classifier unit coverage (`isRetryableLineInboundMediaError`): 202 / 408 / 429 / 5xx / `fetch_failed` → retryable; `404` / `max_bytes` / plain `Error` → not retryable. Download-layer tests assert the raised errors are `MediaFetchError` with the expected `code`/`status`.

Verification (Node 24.15, current main):
- `vitest run … download.test.ts bot-handlers.test.ts` → 44 passed
- `run-tsgo -p tsconfig.extensions.json --noEmit` (source) → clean
- `run-tsgo -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json` (test types) → clean
- `pnpm lint:extensions` → clean
- `oxfmt --check` on the 4 touched files → clean

Diff: `download.ts` +/− (raise `MediaFetchError` + classifier), `bot-handlers.ts` +8 (rethrow branch), plus tests. No plugin-sdk surface, dependency, or lockfile changes.

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway domain for session dashboards (design: `docs/web/dashboard-architecture.md`): sessions get a persistent "board" face that agents compose. This PR delivers the whole server side — protocol schemas and validators, `board.get/update/widget.put/widget.grant/event` RPCs, `board.changed`/`board.command` events, HMAC-ticketed widget serving, the `dashboard` agent tool, tier-1 state-event session notices, and SQLite persistence in the per-agent DB. UI wiring (already landed as #110644/#110728/#110740) connects in the follow-up stitch PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Boards are session state owned by the agent, so storage is the per-agent DB: STRICT `board_tabs`/`board_widgets` with FK cascade and layout/grant checks. Per the new additive-surface rule in AGENTS.md, the schema version stays at 13: tables are declared canonically for fresh DBs and lazily ensured once per DB handle on existing DBs (idempotent DDL, folds into the next natural bump). Downgraded builds keep working — boards are simply absent. Widget iframes authenticate via 2-minute HMAC view tickets bound to session+name+revision+persisted view-generation (no operator token ever reaches sandboxed content); reconstruction-safe (delete/recreate with identical bytes invalidates old tickets). Session reset preserves boards; session deletion removes them. Tool-call parity: the `dashboard` tool covers everything the UI can do, including `focus_tab`/`set_chat_dock` via `board.command`.

## User Impact

No visible surface yet (agent tool + RPCs; UI stitch follows). No config surface added. No schema version bump.

## What Problem This Solves

Widgets rendered in the iOS and macOS chat transcripts are view-only: there is no way to copy or save what the agent drew. Users screenshot manually and crop. Companion to the web export workstream — natively the platforms can do this better.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inline widget card gets platform-native export actions producing a PNG of the rendered widget via `WKWebView.takeSnapshot`:

- macOS: right-click context menu — "Copy image" (NSPasteboard) and "Save image…" (NSSavePanel, default filename from the sanitized widget title).

Snapshot completion stays main-actor isolated and correlates request IDs so overlapping exports cannot race (a finding from review, fixed pre-commit). Filenames are sanitized with a "widget" fallback. Failures surface through the existing alert pattern in `OpenClawChatUI`.

Scope: `apps/shared/OpenClawKit` only; no entitlements, no dependencies, no web/wrapper changes (separate PR).

## User Impact

Long-press (iOS) or right-click (macOS) any widget in the transcript to copy it as an image or save/share it.

target.title: fix(gateway): isolate wizard exits from shared process
target.body:
Closes #110545

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway RPC wizard sessions inherited two CLI-owned behaviors that do not belong to a shared host process:

- setup/channel runners could terminate the Gateway through `runtime.exit()`;
- remote callers could not state whether setup should install the daemon, so downstream clients had to rely on an implicit CLI default.

In the Windows Companion beta.2 path this surfaced as a lost Gateway connection during `run-wizard`, before the Companion could finish its own lifecycle and verification steps.

Downstream consumer: openclaw/openclaw-windows-node#999.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway owns the RPC process and request boundary, so both fixes belong in the same owner seam:

- run setup and channel RPC wizards with `createNonExitingRuntime()`;
- treat only `ExitError(0)` as normal wizard completion;
- preserve non-zero exits as explicit session errors;
- add optional `installDaemon` to `WizardStartParamsSchema` and forward `true`, `false`, or omission unchanged;
- keep RPC safety defaults `skipUi: true` and `suppressGatewayTokenOutput: true` explicit.

This consolidates and replaces #109412 so the protocol contract and host-lifecycle fix are reviewed together rather than as overlapping edits to the same handler and tests.

## User Impact

Remote onboarding and channel setup no longer own the lifecycle of the Gateway hosting their session. Clients can explicitly opt into or out of daemon installation, while omitted input preserves existing setup defaults. Invalid/failing wizard exits remain visible as errors.

## Evidence

Exact proof head: `99b121cf54cfe0aef5413739423bf94059e17398`, merged with current upstream `5590d7c2809496ff88787bbc404d6548601adac7` without force or conflict.

- Official protocol generators ran in a disposable Node 24 Bookworm container pinned to `sha256:5711a0d445a1af54af9589066c646df387d1831a608226f4cd694fc59e745059`.
- `pnpm protocol:check` passed after regenerating the tracked Swift model. Android generated outputs remained byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Repository-supported `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/wizard.test.ts`: 7/7 tests passed. The matrix covers setup/channels exit zero, setup/channels nonzero exit, and explicit `installDaemon` false/true/omission without coercion.
- Repository-supported focused Gateway/WebSocket proof: the two changed lifecycle tests passed 2/2; ten unrelated tests were skipped by the name filter.

target.title: fix(security): add estimate-before-decode guard to base64 paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large base64-encoded images can cause transient memory pressure during decoding. This PR adds a size estimation check before decoding base64 image data in CLI staging, provider image-parsing paths, and the Codex/OpenAI OAuth image-generation result route, and propagates the existing configured media size limit through these new guards.

**Security impact**: Defense-in-depth against transient memory exhaustion from oversized base64 payloads.

## Summary

- Reuses the existing public `estimateBase64DecodedBytes` helper (`@openclaw/media-core/base64`) to estimate decoded byte length before decoding
- Propagates existing `maxBytes` limit through:
  - CLI image writing (`writeCliImages`, in `src/agents/cli-runner/cli-images.ts`)
  - Provider image parsing (`generatedImageAssetFromBase64`)
  - **Codex/OpenAI OAuth image-generation result route** (`parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse` threads `maxBytes`)
- Boundary tests for configured-limit acceptance, over-limit rejection before decode, default-limit enforcement, and Codex OAuth route oversized-entry drop
- **No new configuration**: uses the existing `generatedMediaMaxBytes` setting
- **No new public package API**: the CLI staging guard is a private function in `cli-images.ts` built on the existing `estimateBase64DecodedBytes` export (per review feedback, the earlier `@openclaw/media-core/base64-size-limit` subpath was removed)

## Real behavior proof (final head, 2026-07-19)

Both guarded base64 paths were executed directly on the exact PR head via `tsx` (no mocks — real function calls, real filesystem staging):

```bash
./node_modules/.bin/tsx runtime-proof.mts
```

```text

node: v24.18.0
code path: src/agents/cli-runner/cli-images.ts + src/image-generation/image-assets.ts @ PR head
[cli staging valid] accepted: paths=1 file=/tmp/openclaw/openclaw-cli-images/6a2b0d3f….png
[cli staging over-limit] rejected before decode: Base64 payload exceeds size limit: 40960 bytes > 1024 bytes
[provider parser valid] accepted: assets=1 mime=image/png bytes=70
[provider parser over-limit] rejected before decode: assets=0 (expect 0)
```

- **CLI staging (`writeCliImages`)**: a valid 1×1 PNG under `maxBytes: 1024` is staged to a private file; a 40 KB payload is rejected by the estimate-before-decode guard with a clear size error — `Buffer.from(data, "base64")` is never reached for the over-limit input.
- **Provider parser (`parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse`)**: a valid `b64_json` entry under the budget produces one asset (70 decoded bytes, sniffed `image/png`); the same 40 KB payload is dropped before decode (`assets=0`).

## Regression tests (final head)

## What Problem This Solves

When an ACP backend cancelled a bound turn after partial output reached the user, OpenClaw could omit that output from the bound transcript. The next turn then resumed from history that did not match the conversation.

target.title: fix(install): bound curl connection setup with --connect-timeout 20
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

**Scope reduced after rebase.** Current `main` already bounds post-connect stalls in both installer download helpers with `--speed-limit 1 --speed-time 30` (30-second low-speed grace window). This PR now adds only the remaining gap: `--connect-timeout 20`.

The stall-sensitive `--speed-limit`/`--speed-time` options only take effect **after the connection is established**. If the release host is blackholed or unresponsive during connection setup (SYN sent, no reply), curl hangs in the connect phase indefinitely — blocking first-time installs and `openclaw` upgrades. The wget sibling already covers this phase via `--timeout=20`, which applies to connection establishment as well.

## Why This Change Was Made

`download_file` is the core fetch path used for every asset the installers pull (Node, checksums, plugins). curl's timeout model splits into two phases:

- **Connect phase**: governed only by `--connect-timeout` — previously unbounded in the curl branch.
- **Transfer phase**: already governed on main by `--speed-limit 1 --speed-time 30` (abort only if speed stays below 1 byte/s for 30 seconds).

Adding `--connect-timeout 20` bounds the connect phase without imposing any total download duration, so slow-but-progressing downloads remain unaffected. The existing 30-second low-speed grace window is preserved exactly as on main.

## User Impact

- Normal installs: no behavior change.
- Slow but healthy networks: no behavior change (no hard total time limit; 30s grace window unchanged).
- Blackholed/unresponsive host during connect: fails after ~20 seconds (matching the wget branch's `--timeout=20` connection window) instead of hanging forever.
- Post-connect stall: unchanged from main — aborts after 30 seconds below 1 byte/s.

## Evidence

All runs use the exact flags now in `scripts/install.sh` / `scripts/install-cli.sh`:
`--connect-timeout 20 --speed-limit 1 --speed-time 30` (with `-fsSL`; `--retry` omitted in proofs so a single attempt is measured).

### Proof A — normal download succeeds

```
=== Proof A: normal download with exact flags ===

real    0m1.220s
exit=0 size=87538 bytes
```

(`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openclaw/openclaw/main/README.md`)

### Proof B — slow but progressing download is NOT killed

Local server trickling 100 bytes at ~5 bytes/s (above the 1 byte/s threshold, transfer takes ~20s):

```

real    0m19.084s
exit=0 size=100 bytes (expect 100)
```

### Proof C — post-connect stall is aborted at ~30s

Local server sends a partial body, then goes silent:

```

curl: (28) Operation too slow. Less than 1 bytes/sec transferred the last 30 seconds
exit=28 (expect 28)
2026年 7月19日 星期日 06时48分06秒 CST
```

### Proof D — blackholed connect is bounded by --connect-timeout 20

Non-routable address `10.255.255.1:81` (proxy bypassed with `--noproxy '*'` so the connect phase itself is measured):

```

curl: (28) Failed to connect to 10.255.255.1 port 81 after 20006 ms: Timeout was reached

real    0m20.025s
exit=28 (expect 28)
2026年 7月19日 星期日 08时05分21秒 CST
```

### Regression tests

```
pnpm test test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts test/scripts/install-cli.test.ts --run
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  113 passed (113)
```

(The stubbed-curl assertions in both test files now require `--connect-timeout 20` alongside the unchanged `--speed-limit 1 --speed-time 30`.)

## What was not tested

- Full installer end-to-end run (Node/plugin downloads) — the change is confined to curl flags in `download_file`; behavior proven at the exact-flag level above.
- wget branch — untouched (`--timeout=20` already bounds connect).

---

**Summary of scope reduction:** the original `--max-time 60` / 20s-stall-window versions of this PR are superseded by main's 30s stall-window fix. This PR is rebased onto main and now adds `--connect-timeout 20` (matching the wget branch's `--timeout=20` connection window, per review feedback) to `scripts/install.sh` and `scripts/install-cli.sh`, plus matching test assertions.

## What Problem This Solves

When an agent's display name begins with an emoji or other astral Unicode character, the Control UI renders a broken/garbled avatar initial (a lone UTF-16 surrogate half) instead of the intended glyph, because the fallback uses `.slice(0, 1)` / `[0]` (first UTF-16 code unit).

No second grapheme implementation remains.
- **The four live avatar fallback surfaces** now route through that owner via `deriveAvatarInitial(...) || "?"`:

target.title: fix: release stream reader lock, bound error body reads, cancel cloned body
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes three issues where HTTP response bodies are not properly cleaned up or bounded in failure paths:

1. **Ollama stream reader lock never released**: response.body.getReader() lock is never released, relying solely on implicit fetch cleanup which can delay socket reuse in some Node.js versions.
2. **HTTP error body read without byte limit**: The readResponseBodySnippet fallback uses unbounded response.text(), risking OOM on large error responses from reverse proxies.
3. **Firecrawl error-path body not explicitly cancelled**: After cloning and consuming a response body for JSON error parsing, the original body is not explicitly cancelled.

## Why This Change Was Made

- ollama/stream.ts: Added reader.releaseLock() in the finally block before release()
- http-error-body.ts: Replaced response.text() with bounded response.arrayBuffer() + subarray() capping at limits.maxBytes
- firecrawl-client.ts: Added response.body?.cancel() after successful clone consumption

## User Impact

Gateway and plugin processes no longer leak stream resources or risk large memory allocations on error responses. Connection pools recover faster after Ollama/Firecrawl failures.

## Evidence

Three targeted, single-site changes. No modification to success-path behavior.

target.title: feat(config): add compaction.thinkingLevel to override thinking level during compaction
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Embedded compaction inherited the active turn's thinking level, so operators could not tune summary cost and quality independently from ordinary turns.

## Why This Change Was Made

The maintainer rewrite adds the optional `agents.defaults.compaction.thinkingLevel` setting across the exported config type, schema, help metadata, generated plugin SDK baseline, and docs. All nine supported thinking levels are accepted.

For embedded compaction, the configured override wins over the inherited turn level, then is revalidated and clamped for every concrete provider, model, and runtime candidate, including fallbacks. When unset, existing inherited behavior is preserved.

Native Codex app-server compaction warns and ignores this setting because the upstream compact operation currently exposes only a thread identifier and has no per-operation reasoning parameter.

## User Impact

Operators can use a lower or higher reasoning level for embedded compaction without changing ordinary turns, while unsupported levels are handled by the same capability-aware resolver as normal model selection.

## Release Note

Agent defaults now support `compaction.thinkingLevel` for embedded compaction summaries, with concrete-model validation and an explicit warning for native Codex compaction. Thanks @mpz4life.

## Evidence

- Exact reviewed head: `05fe325609352`
- Blacksmith Testbox: 150 focused config, schema-help, embedded compaction, and Codex compact tests passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox: full changed gates passed in 15m56.86s.
- Blacksmith Testbox: 235 declaration contracts, the complete test-type gate, and all 10 plugin SDK surface-report tests passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox: the final combined-main plugin SDK surface and generated API baseline checks passed; surface and baseline suites passed 16 tests.
- Blacksmith Testbox: the latest-main plugin SDK surface and generated API baseline checks passed again.
- Fresh branch autoreview after the latest main merge: no findings, confidence 0.90.
- Exact-head hosted CI is running on the final source/test diff.

## Compatibility / Migration

The field is additive and optional; unset configuration preserves existing behavior. No migration is required. Native Codex behavior is documented rather than simulated with an OpenClaw-side shim.

target.title: fix: carry reply metadata into runtime context
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram/forum reply facts can exist in channel context but be lost or persisted as user-authored prompt text before they reach the active model runtime. The runtime needs structured current-turn reply metadata without leaking replied-to message bodies into trusted metadata or transcript text.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add structured current-message, thread, reply-target, quote, and reply-chain identifiers to `CurrentInboundPromptContext`.
- Keep replied-to body text out of the trusted metadata block and verbose trace.
- Route reply metadata through hidden embedded runtime context while leaving `promptForSession` / `promptForModel` as the user-authored prompt.
- Preserve current-main heartbeat outcome and prepared-timestamp behavior during the rebase.
- Carry the same reply metadata into CLI runtime input while keeping the CLI transcript prompt clean.
- Use the same bare marker prompt for runtime-only turns and place inbound metadata in runtime system context.

## User Impact

Agents can reason about what a Telegram/forum message replies to without polluting stored user prompts or losing reply/thread identity across embedded and CLI runtime paths.

## Evidence

Current contributor head: `56db6549677` on upstream `main` `e5b2ca3c6bd`.

- Focused current-branch run: 5 test files across unit/agent projects, 212 tests passed.
- Positive coverage: structured reply metadata reaches embedded hidden runtime context and CLI runtime input, including runtime-only room events.
- Negative coverage: replied-to body text is excluded; visible/model/transcript prompts remain the user-authored text; quote presence and generic reply-target presence stay distinct.
- Cross-runtime regression explicitly verifies CLI prompt availability while `transcriptPrompt` and context-engine turn prompt remain clean.
- Direct formatter check and `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.
- The pre-PR plan gate passed for core/runtime test lanes with no dependency-sensitive changes.

### Real behavior proof

Earlier redacted Telegram/forum transport supplied real message/thread/reply identifiers and confirmed that the persisted session user message remained user-authored text only. The current-head tests drive the real prompt-envelope, runtime-context split, embedded attempt assembly, context-engine handoff, and CLI prepare path.

No live Telegram bot round-trip was deployed on this exact rebased head. No Gateway restart or production session migration was performed. The remaining live-transport step is optional maintainer/Mantis confirmation; the branch-specific runtime boundary is covered directly.

Addresses the runtime-handoff portion of #88032.

AI-assisted; reviewed and validated before submission.

target.title: fix(gateway): make scope errors machine-readable across clients
target.body:
Follow-up to #110925

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where gateway clients could receive machine-readable missing-scope details from the server but still had to parse the human message, or misclassified a permanent authorization failure as bad parameters or a transient error. Parameter-dependent methods also duplicated scope policy between dispatch and handlers, which made regressions easy: reset-style agent requests, privileged node invokes, and unredacted talk configuration did not share one authorization owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a browser-safe protocol reader that prefers `details.code = MISSING_SCOPE` while retaining the existing message and legacy fallback, then migrates the CLI, probe/status paths, Control UI, Android, and Apple clients to it. Dynamic method scope requirements now live in the pre-dispatch method policy and are reused by handler defenses; direct invocation and pairing share one admin-only node-command classifier, while the persistent browser mutation guard remains fail-closed at its more precise handler boundary.

The Android error model now preserves generic gateway details instead of naming connect-only details, and both mobile clients clear stale operator-question state when `operator.questions` is unavailable. The protocol and operator-scope docs cover the additive contract and parameter-dependent scopes.

## User Impact

Third-party and first-party clients can give actionable missing-permission guidance without regexing `missing scope: ...`. Existing clients keep working because the message string and legacy parsing fallback remain intact. Operators also get consistent `FORBIDDEN` semantics for parameter-dependent scope failures instead of ambiguous `INVALID_REQUEST` handling.

Release-note context: gateway clients can now consume structured missing-scope details across method-level authorization failures, with legacy message compatibility retained.

## Evidence

- `pnpm check:changed` passed on Blacksmith Testbox, including generated protocol/API baselines, all TypeScript typechecks, full core/package lint, import-cycle and boundary guards, and macOS packaging tests.
- Before the final main rebase, 273 focused gateway/protocol/UI/CLI tests passed; `@openclaw/gateway-protocol` and `@openclaw/gateway-client` package builds passed.
- Before the final main rebase, Android `ktlintCheck` and targeted `GatewayErrorDetailsTest`, `ChatQuestionTest`, and `GatewaySessionReconnectTest` passed.
- `/tools` ownership-boundary follow-up: 31 `commands-info` tests passed.
- Current exact head passed `native:i18n:check`, the changed node-pairing test (15 assertions), all test typechecks, production/full-tree/script dead-code export scans, script-declaration validation, and targeted formatting.
- Real provider proof: OpenAI Responses streaming test passed with the Molty-managed `OPENAI_API_KEY` on direct AWS Crabbox run `run_90c1f5464f1c` (`cbx_63d01e15905d`); the lease was stopped and the key was not printed.
- Apple shared-package tests could not run on Linux because upstream SwiftMath/CoreGraphics and SQLite3 modules are platform-bound; native Apple CI is required before merge.
- Multi-pass autoreview found and drove the node-pairing policy unification, then finished clean with no accepted/actionable findings (0.92 confidence).

- [x] AI-assisted
- [x] I understand the change and verified the affected ownership boundaries.

target.title: Bound trajectory pointer file read with size cap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readTrajectoryPointerFile` calls `fs.readFileSync(pointerPath, "utf8")` on session trajectory pointer files with no size limit. A corrupted pointer file can OOM the trajectory cleanup path.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #101472 established the bounded-read pattern for file reads. Trajectory pointer files are small JSON metadata files, but the unbounded `readFileSync` call was a latent vulnerability. Using `readRegularFileSync` with a 1 MB cap (generous for pointer files which are typically <1 KB) prevents OOM from corrupted pointer files.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Trajectory pointer files are small JSON objects (<1 KB typically); a 1 MB cap is more than sufficient. Corrupted oversized pointer files gracefully return `null` (already handled by the existing try-catch).

## Evidence

- Replaced `fs.readFileSync(pointerPath, "utf8")` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath: pointerPath, maxBytes: TRAJECTORY_POINTER_MAX_BYTES })` at `src/trajectory/cleanup.ts:65-69`
- Added `TRAJECTORY_POINTER_MAX_BYTES = 1 * 1024 * 1024` constant
- Added `readRegularFileSync` import from `../infra/regular-file.js`

target.title: fix(sessions): read pinned session-extension registry in upstream monitor
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The session upstream monitor resolved catalog providers from the **mutable** plugin registry state (`getPluginRegistryState()?.activeRegistry`). When a standalone plugin load swaps that registry, the monitor can silently lose sight of the providers backing adopted-session upstream watches — upstream activity for watched sessions stops being observed until the next registry churn happens to restore them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Switch the monitor's provider source to the **pinned** session-extension registry (`getActivePluginSessionExtensionRegistry`), the same source the session-catalog path already trusts. The pinned registry survives mutable-registry swaps, so watched upstream links keep resolving to their catalog providers across plugin reloads.

## User Impact

Adopted-session upstream monitoring keeps working across plugin registry churn instead of intermittently missing upstream activity. No configuration or API change.

## Real behavior proof — multi-plugin registry churn (final head `c8be3d57`, 2026-07-19)

Runtime trace executing the **real** plugin runtime (`src/plugins/runtime.ts`), state database (SQLite in a temp state dir), and the real monitor tick (`src/sessions/session-upstream-monitor.ts`) — no mocks of the monitor or registry plumbing. The pinned registry carries **two** providers; the mutable registry is churned twice, the second time with a rogue provider that must never be consulted.

```bash
./node_modules/.bin/tsx registry-churn-proof.mts
```

target.title: fix(e2e): bound non-root installer fetch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The non-root install-sh Docker smoke runner fetches the official installer and pipes it straight into bash. Current `origin/main` bounds that pipe with `--connect-timeout 30 --max-time 300`, but it still streams the payload directly into the shell and uses a much looser budget than the sibling e2e runner:

```sh
# scripts/docker/install-sh-nonroot/run.sh (current origin/main)
curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 300 -- "$INSTALL_URL" | bash
```

This PR brings the non-root runner to the same **download-then-execute** contract as the sibling e2e runner merged in #108810 (`scripts/docker/install-sh-e2e/run.sh`): download the installer to a temp file with explicit connect/total timeouts, verify curl completed, then execute it, then clean up.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Fail fast on stall:** `--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120` matches the values already merged for the sibling installer/download fixes in this area (#108810, #108911). A stalled fetch fails the step in under 2 minutes instead of tying up the runner for 5.
- **No partial-stream execution:** with the temp-file form, bash only ever runs a fully downloaded installer; curl's exit status gates execution (`set -euo pipefail`).
- **Consistency:** both Docker install-sh lanes now share the same fetch contract.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change to the installer itself. This only affects the non-root install-sh Docker CI lane: a stalled installer download fails fast with a clear curl error instead of streaming into a long-hanging pipe. Identical install semantics on success.

## Evidence

After (this PR, `scripts/docker/install-sh-nonroot/run.sh`):

```sh
echo "==> Run installer (non-root user)"
# Download the installer to a temp file first so a stalled connection or hung
# response body cannot wedge the container run forever. Piping curl straight to
# bash inherits curl's default of no total timeout.
installer="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$installer"' EXIT
curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o "$installer" "$INSTALL_URL"
bash "$installer"
```

Regression tests (final head `15ad709b`, rebased onto latest main):

```bash
pnpm vitest run test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts
```

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  77 passed (77)
```

Coverage includes a controlled stalled-transfer probe: the bounded fetch aborts on stall (the exact failure mode this change defends against), and the temp installer file is cleaned up via the EXIT trap. The runner-assertion test now checks the bounded temp-file form (`--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o "$installer"` + `bash "$installer"`).

## What was not tested

A live successful non-root **Docker** smoke run against the real installer endpoint: this contributor environment has no container runtime, so no Docker transcript is attached. Behavior on the success path is unchanged apart from the fetch budget (curl flags and execution order are asserted by the suite above); the stall path is proven hermetically.

## CI note

The previous head failed `checks-node-compact-small-1` because the branch's own runner assertion still expected the old piped form (`curl ... | bash`) that this PR replaces. The assertion is aligned with the temp-file fetch on the current head, and the branch is rebased onto latest main.

target.title: Plan grouped Claw agent updates
target.body:
## Summary

- add `openclaw.clawUpdatePlan.v1` for read-only, agent-centric reconciliation of a grouped Claw manifest
- add `openclaw claws update <claw-or-agent> [--from <source>] --dry-run [--json]` behind `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`
- resolve the normal target from persisted add provenance; keep `--from` as an explicit override and recovery path
- compare effective agent capabilities, workspace files, exact package refs, MCP declarations, and agent-pinned cron declarations
- bind the complete preview to `planIntegrity` for the consented apply slice
- perform no mutation: planning opens existing state read-only, does not create or migrate databases, and closes every owned handle

## Planning contract

- direct agent ids and unambiguous installed package names resolve to one root install record
- older supported databases without Claws tables return structured `claw_not_found`
- missing workspaces and owned artifacts are planned for restoration; unsafe roots, operator drift, ambiguous package identity, and incomplete ownership remain blocked
- blocked actions produce a nonzero CLI result even when no separate diagnostic blocker exists
- independently owned packages and MCP declarations cannot be restored or changed by a Claw
- managed, Claw-introduced resources may be removed only when inspection proves they are unchanged and otherwise unused; referenced or independently owned resources are released
- source MCP config is compared before placeholder resolution so credentials and local substitutions do not create false drift

## Capability and consent contract

- capability changes use secret-safe summaries plus SHA-256 digests; raw MCP configuration and cron payloads never enter the plan model
- effective sandbox values come from OpenClaw's production resolver, including inherited defaults
- widening workspace access, sandbox sharing, tool access, plugin code, MCP surfaces, or scheduled automation requires distinct escalation consent
- reductions and blocked removals do not request escalation consent

## Real behavior proof

Current head: `0eef342ada1275d02142d4702803c09957a9c664`.

An isolated v1 Claw was added with integrity-bound consent, then v2 introduced a remote OAuth MCP URL containing `URL_SECRET_123`, a secret-like tool filter, and cron message `CRON_SECRET_ABC`.

Human preview:

```text
Claw update plan: @proof/safe-preview 1.0.0 -> 2.0.0
Agent: safe-preview
Update actions: 4
Capability changes: 5; escalations requiring distinct consent: 3
  - agent.sandbox.mode: off -> all (change)
  - agent.sandbox.scope: agent -> session (change)
  ! agent.sandbox.workspaceAccess: none -> ro (change)
  ! cronJobs.private-report: unset -> schedule cron; session isolated; payload withheld (add)
  ! mcpServers.private-search: unset -> remote server; auth configured; tool filter configured (add)
```

JSON emitted only paths, classifications, summaries, and digests. It contained none of `secret.example.test`, `URL_SECRET_123`, `PRIVATE_TOOL_SECRET_456`, or `CRON_SECRET_ABC`.

## Verification

- focused update planner and CLI: 46 tests passed
- real Claw lifecycle E2E: 8 tests passed

## What Problem This Solves

The `extensionSourceNeedsJitiAliasResolution` function reads entire extension source files into memory with no size bound. Extension source files can be large (compiled bundles, bundled dependencies), risking OOM.

1. Verifies the path is a regular file
2. Rejects files exceeding 10 MiB by returning `true` (assumes jiti alias resolution is needed)
3. Only then reads content with `readFileSync` and scans for import patterns

target.title: fix(grep): bound file reads with size cap in default grep operations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The default `readFile` operation in the grep tool reads files with no size bound. When grep matches lines in a large file (e.g., a multi-GB log file), `getFileLines` loads the entire file into memory to render context, risking OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `defaultGrepOperations.readFile` function used raw `readFileSync(p, "utf-8")` with no size pre-check. The fix adds a `statSync` pre-check that:

1. Verifies the path is a regular file (not a directory or device)
2. Rejects files exceeding 50 MiB with a clear error
3. Only then reads content with `readFileSync`

The error is caught by `getFileLines`, which returns empty lines on error — the same graceful degradation as other read failures (e.g. permission errors).

## User Impact

- Prevents OOM crashes when grep matches lines in oversized files
- Context lines for oversized files render as `<path>:<line>: (unable to read file)` — the match itself is still reported, only the surrounding-context rendering is omitted
- No change for normal files under 50 MiB

## Evidence

**Focused tests** — `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sessions/tools/grep.stream-errors.test.ts src/agents/sessions/tools/grep-bound-read.test.ts` — 12/12 pass:

```text
 ✓ |agents| src/agents/sessions/tools/grep.stream-errors.test.ts (8 tests)
 ✓ |agents| src/agents/sessions/tools/grep-bound-read.test.ts (4 tests)
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  12 passed (12)
```

The new `grep-bound-read.test.ts` imports the real `defaultGrepOperations` and exercises its actual `readFile` for directory rejection, over-cap rejection, under-cap content return, and the exact 50 MiB boundary (strict `>` comparison).

**Knip (`deadcode:full`, both scans)** — production scan and all-exports scan both exit 0. `defaultGrepOperations` carries `/** @internal Exported for testing */`, the existing repo pattern for test-only exports (same as `parseModelPattern` in `src/agents/sessions/model-resolver.ts`): the production knip scan ignores `@internal` exports, and the all-exports scan counts the test file import as usage.

## Real Behavior Proof

Run on the pushed head `af2662120fdc5b07937f5b0b12ced49d06ba33dc` using the real default grep tool — `createGrepToolDefinition(cwd)` with **no custom operations** (the same construction the session tool registry uses in `src/agents/sessions/tools/index.ts`) — against an isolated scenario directory:

- `oversized.log` — 53,000,000 bytes (> 50 MiB = 52,428,800) with a `GREP_PROOF_NEEDLE` match on line 1
- `normal.log` — 127 bytes with the same needle surrounded by context lines

Redacted terminal transcript (`<home>` = local user home, scenario under `/tmp`):

```text
$ git rev-parse HEAD
af2662120fdc5b07937f5b0b12ced49d06ba33dc

$ git log -1 --oneline
af2662120fd fix(grep): tag test-only defaultGrepOperations export as @internal for knip

$ ls -l /tmp/openclaw-grep-proof-scenario
total 51764
-rw-rw-r-- 1 <user> <user>      127 Jul 19 08:29 normal.log
-rw-rw-r-- 1 <user> <user> 53000000 Jul 19 08:29 oversized.log

$ stat -c "%n %s bytes" /tmp/openclaw-grep-proof-scenario/*.log
/tmp/openclaw-grep-proof-scenario/normal.log 127 bytes
/tmp/openclaw-grep-proof-scenario/oversized.log 53000000 bytes

$ node --import tsx .tmp/grep-proof/driver.mts /tmp/openclaw-grep-proof-scenario /tmp/openclaw-grep-proof-scenario/oversized.log
direct readFile(oversized.log) threw: file too large (53000000 bytes > 52428800 byte limit): /tmp/openclaw-grep-proof-scenario/oversized.log
--- default grep tool output (context=2) ---
normal.log-1- before context line 1
normal.log-2- before context line 2
normal.log:3: GREP_PROOF_NEEDLE inside the normal file
normal.log-4- after context line 1
normal.log-5- after context line 2
oversized.log:1: (unable to read file)
--- tool run completed without crashing ---
exit code: 0
```

Observed on the current head:

1. The real default context reader rejects the oversized file before reading: `file too large (53000000 bytes > 52428800 byte limit)`.
2. In the full default grep run (real ripgrep spawn, `context=2`), the match in `oversized.log` degrades to bounded empty context — `oversized.log:1: (unable to read file)` — instead of loading 53 MB into memory.
3. The match in `normal.log` retains its full surrounding context (`normal.log-1-` through `normal.log-5-`).
4. The tool run completes successfully (exit code 0); grep keeps working normally for all other files.

## Degraded-Behavior Contract (maintainer confirmation requested)

Answering the review's maintainer-decision question explicitly: this PR intentionally establishes that matching regular files **over a fixed 50 MiB threshold** return **no context lines** through the existing read-error degradation path (`(unable to read file)`), rather than implementing a bounded/streaming context extraction for large files. Rationale: it is the smallest change that removes the unbounded-read OOM risk, it reuses the already-shipped degradation path used for every other read failure, and the match itself is still reported. Files exactly at 50 MiB are still read (strict `>`), and files under the cap are completely unaffected. target.title: fix(sessions): bound AGENTS.md and prompt-input file reads with size cap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two file read paths in the session resource loader read files without any size bound, risking OOM from large or corrupted files:

1. **`resolvePromptInput`** — reads user-supplied `--system-prompt` and `--append-system-prompt` files with unbounded `readFileSync`. A user could accidentally (or maliciously) point this at a multi-GB file, exhausting memory.

2. **`loadContextFileFromDir`** — reads `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` project context files with unbounded `readFileSync`. These files are user-authored and can be arbitrarily large.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both paths use raw `fs.readFileSync` with no limit on file size. The fix adds a `readTextFileSafely` helper that:

1. `statSync` the file first to check it is a regular file
2. Rejects files exceeding the byte cap with a clear warning
3. Only then reads content with `readFileSync`

Caps:
- **AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md context files**: 1 MiB — these are project metadata files, not meant to be large
- **User-supplied prompt input files**: 10 MiB — these can include larger instructions but still capped

## User Impact

- Prevents OOM crashes from oversized input files during session startup
- Preserves warning logs for non-regular-file paths (directories, devices)
- Gracefully skips oversized files instead of crashing the process

## Evidence

**`pnpm test src/agents/sessions/resource-loader.test.ts`** — all 5 tests pass:

- "does not use unreadable prompt file paths as prompt content" — existing test preserved
- "rejects oversized system prompt files" — 11 MiB file rejected with warning
- "accepts system prompt files within the byte limit" — normal file loads correctly
- "skips oversized AGENTS.md files during context file loading" — 2 MiB AGENTS.md skipped
- "loads AGENTS.md files within the byte limit" — normal AGENTS.md loads correctly

target.title: fix(qa-lab): cancel unread response body in crabline injection
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #109992

**What changed**: Added `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the `throw` in the `postCrablineInbound()` error path. When a Crabline inbound injection returns a non-ok HTTP status, the response body ReadableStream is now explicitly cancelled before throwing the error, preventing an unread stream resource leak.

**What NOT changed**: No change to the happy path — successful responses still pass through to the complete handler as before. No change to the Crabline injection logic, request construction, or error message format. No new dependencies added.

**merge-risk**: Minimal — the pattern `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` is a standard no-op on success and a no-throw guard on failure. It affects only the single error path in `crabline-transport.ts`. Zero risk of regression on the ok path.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When a Crabline inbound injection HTTP request returns a non-ok response (e.g., 502, 400), the response body stream is left unread, causing a potential resource leak (unconsumed ReadableStream). Node.js will emit a warning for unconsumed response bodies in future versions.

**Root Cause**: `postCrablineInbound()` throws immediately in the `if (!response.ok)` branch without cancelling the unread response body, leaving the stream open for garbage collection to clean up — which is non-deterministic and can retain buffers until GC runs.

**Solution**: Add `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the `throw` in the error path to eagerly release the stream. The `cancel()` method (Fetch API standard) releases the stream's resources. The `?.` optional chaining guards against a null body (e.g., 204 No Content responses or server errors that omit a body). The `.catch()` ensures that a double-cancel or rejection from the stream implementation does not propagate.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: When a Crabline inbound injection receives a non-ok HTTP response (e.g., 502, 400), the response body stream is now explicitly cancelled before the error is thrown, eliminating a resource leak from an unconsumed ReadableStream.

## Summary

`loadRuntimeParityMockToolCalls` fetches the `debug/requests` endpoint from a configured QA Lab runtime parity server. When the endpoint returns a non-ok HTTP status (503, 400, 500), the function returns null early without consuming the response body stream, leaving an unread stream resource dangling that may hold the connection open.

The fix adds `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the early return on `!response.ok`. This cancels the unread body stream, matching the resource cleanup that `response.json()` implicitly performs on the ok path.

**What changed**: One line added in `loadRuntimeParityMockToolCalls` at `runtime-parity.ts:1055`. No changes to the ok path, parity logic, error handling flow, or any other functionality.

**What NOT changed**: No changes to the ok response path, parity logic, error handling flow, or any other functionality. No new dependencies or configuration options added.

Fixes #109991

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: `loadRuntimeParityMockToolCalls` returns null early on non-ok HTTP responses without cancelling the unread response body stream, potentially leaking resources and holding connections open.

**Root Cause**: At `runtime-parity.ts:1055`, the `!response.ok` early-return path calls `return null` without first cancelling the response body stream via `response.body?.cancel()`. The ok path implicitly drains the body via `response.json()`, but the non-ok path has no such cleanup.

**Solution**: Add `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before returning null on non-ok responses. This mirrors the resource cleanup that `response.json()` implicitly performs on the ok path. The `.catch(() => undefined)` guard ensures safety even if the body stream is already in an inconsistent state.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(qa-lab): cancel unread response body on HTTP error + fix(vertex-adc): guard JSON.parse
target.body:
## Summary

**What changed**: Two fixes in this PR.

1. **qa-lab: cancel unread response body on HTTP error** — Add `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before throwing on non-2xx responses in `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` so the connection is released back to the pool.
2. **vertex-adc: guard JSON.parse against malformed credential files** — Wrap `JSON.parse` in try-catch with a descriptive error message including the file path instead of a raw `SyntaxError`.

**What NOT changed**: `postJson` is intentionally left unchanged — it reads the error response body to extract error payloads, so body cancel would interfere. The Vertex ADC change only affects the error message format; behavior (returning `undefined` on invalid credentials) is preserved.

Fixes #109985

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**:
- QA Lab HTTP: When `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` receive a non-2xx HTTP status, they throw without consuming the response body. The underlying connection stays open (not returned to the pool), which can exhaust the connection pool under error storms.
- Vertex ADC: A malformed credential file at `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` causes a raw `SyntaxError` from `JSON.parse`, giving users no indication of which file is broken.

**Root Cause**:
- QA Lab HTTP: `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` call `response.json()` only on success. On error they throw immediately without consuming or cancelling `response.body`. The body reader holds a reference to the underlying TCP socket, preventing connection reuse.
- Vertex ADC: `readGoogleAdcCredentials` calls `JSON.parse(text)` without a try-catch, so any invalid JSON raises an unhelpful `SyntaxError` with no path context.

**Solution**:
- QA Lab HTTP: Insert `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the `throw` in both `getJson` and `getJsonNoStore`. Optional chaining handles null body; `.catch()` suppresses cancellation rejections.
- Vertex ADC: Wrap `JSON.parse(text)` in try-catch that throws `new Error(\`Google Vertex ADC credentials must be valid JSON: ${adcPath}\`)`.

## Evidence

### Fix 1: QA Lab HTTP body cancel

**Real environment tested**:
Node.js 22, vitest 4.1.10, Linux 6.17.0-40-generic

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
npx vitest run extensions/qa-lab/web/src/http.evidence.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```

 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJson 403: body cancelled 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJson 500: body cancelled 1ms
```

## Summary

Fixes #109983

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When auth fails in Telegram Mini App, the response body stream is left unconsumed, which can cause resource leaks or unhandled rejections in the fetch runtime.

**Root Cause**: The `renderTelegramMiniAppPage` function checks `response.ok` and throws immediately on non-ok status without calling `response.body.cancel()`, leaving the body stream dangling.

**Solution**: Call `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before throwing the auth error to properly release the stream.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Local test server serving 401 response, simulating Telegram Mini App auth error.

```
PASS: repeated cancel() is idempotent
ALL CHECKS PASSED
```

target.title: fix(imessage): prevent duplicate messages after delayed sends
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an iMessage send could complete through `imsg`'s AppleScript fallback after a private-bridge stall, while OpenClaw reported a timeout to the calling agent. The agent then retried the apparently failed send, producing duplicate messages.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dedicated send timeout is increased from 150 seconds to 180 seconds. This lets the outer RPC outlive `imsg`'s 150-second bridge deadline plus its fallback verification window, while leaving the 10-second probe timeout unchanged.

This is intentionally a boundary fix rather than a second delivery-verification implementation in OpenClaw. In the observed incident, the delivered rows stored their text in `attributedBody`, so OpenClaw's plain `message.text` recovery path could not reliably identify them. `imsg` already owns that verification.

## User Impact

Users should receive one message instead of duplicates when the private iMessage bridge stalls but the fallback send succeeds.

## Evidence

### Redacted live failure timeline before the fix

One cron session issued three sends of the same text to the same chat:

```text
09:00:33  send request 1 started
09:03:14  OpenClaw reported imsg rpc timeout (send); outgoing row 7080 persisted
09:03:19  calling agent retried
09:05:57  OpenClaw reported imsg rpc timeout (send); outgoing row 7081 persisted
09:06:19  calling agent used direct imsg send; outgoing row 7082 persisted
```

Recipient and message text are omitted. The matching timeout and persistence timestamps show that the first two sends completed at the point the 150-second outer timer rejected them.

### Dependency and caller contract

- `imsg` assigns send actions a [150-second bridge deadline](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/IMsgCore/IMsgBridgeProtocol.swift#L28-L39), which its [bridge client enforces](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/IMsgCore/IMsgBridgeClient.swift#L97-L121).
- Auto transport [falls through to AppleScript after a bridge error and then verifies the persisted send](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/imsg/RPCServer%2BHandlers.swift#L271-L320).
- The persisted-message verifier [polls for up to 8 seconds](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/imsg/SentMessageVerifier.swift#L13-L26).
- OpenClaw selects the dedicated default in [`sendMessageIMessage`](https://github.com/omarshahine/openclaw/blob/fce7399810c/extensions/imessage/src/send.ts#L720-L725) and [passes it to the single RPC request](https://github.com/omarshahine/openclaw/blob/fce7399810c/extensions/imessage/src/send.ts#L871-L885). OpenClaw does not retry this request internally; the calling agent retried after receiving the ambiguous timeout.

### Deterministic delayed-boundary proof

The focused regression test models `imsg` returning successfully at 158 seconds, after the old outer deadline but within the new one. It asserts that the send resolves with the fallback message GUID and that OpenClaw makes exactly one RPC request.

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       52 passed (52)
```

Command: `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/imessage/src/send.test.ts`

### Live patched-build proof

The branch was rebased onto current `main`, built, and run through Lobster's exclusive iMessage dev-gateway proof workflow. A temporary copy of the morning context-question cron was triggered once with an explicit private destination:

```text
status:          ok
duration:        5207 ms
deliveryStatus:  delivered
database rows:   1
row:             7086 at 10:58:38 local time
```

The recipient, message text, and GUID are omitted. The unique output persisted as exactly one outgoing row. This live run completed through the normal fast bridge path; the 158-second fallback boundary is covered deterministically above because forcing a real bridge stall would require restarting Messages with a stale readiness marker and would introduce an avoidable delivery race.

After proof, the temporary dev cron was removed, the dev gateway stopped, and production was restored healthy on port 18789 with exactly one `imsg rpc` process.

Additional validation:

- Full branch build passed on current `main`.
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Final Codex branch autoreview: no findings; patch rated correct with 0.94 confidence.

AI-assisted: diagnosis, implementation, test updates, and independent review were performed with Codex under maintainer supervision.

target.title: fix(openai-http): keep SSE argument chunking UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

Replace `String.prototype.slice()` with `sliceUtf16Safe()` in `splitArgumentsForStreaming` to prevent SSE argument chunks from splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs. The old code could produce invalid JSON when multi-byte characters (e.g., CJK, emoji) straddled the 256-char chunk boundary, causing downstream parse failures on the client.

Fixes #110642

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: SSE streaming chunks of tool_call arguments can contain truncated/invalid UTF-16 when the 256-char boundary falls inside a surrogate pair, causing the client to receive malformed JSON.

**Root Cause**: `splitArgumentsForStreaming()` in `src/gateway/openai-http.ts` uses `String.prototype.slice()` which operates on UTF-16 code units without awareness of surrogate pairs. When a multi-byte character spans positions 255-256, the slice produces a broken chunk.

**Solution**: Import and use `sliceUtf16Safe()` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`, which ensures surrogate pairs are never split. The loop increment is changed from a fixed `+= chunkSize` to `+= chunk.length` (with `|| 1` fallback) because the safe slice may return 256 or 257 characters.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: SSE chunking of tool_call arguments to not split UTF-16 surrogate pairs

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-40-generic / vitest 4.1.10 / OpenClaw worktree

target.title: fix(doctor): guard snapshot store load against corrupt JSON
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadSessionStoreForSnapshotScan` had a broad catch that silently swallowed all errors from corrupt JSON or unreadable snapshot stores, returning `{}`. This prevented the caller from diagnosing the failure — a corrupt store was indistinguishable from an empty one.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inner try/catch merged two distinct failure modes (corrupt JSON, unreadable file) into a silent empty result. The caller `detectSessionSnapshotHealthIssues` already had a catch boundary, but it was dead code because the inner function never threw. This fix:
1. Removes the inner catch so JSON parse / filesystem errors propagate naturally
2. The caller catch at `detectSessionSnapshotHealthIssues` now handles the error instead of being dead code

Now a corrupt or unreadable snapshot store produces a visible diagnostic while continuing to scan other stores.

## User Impact

Prevents silent skipping of corrupt snapshot stores during `openclaw doctor` session snapshot health checks. The user now sees a clear diagnostic when a store cannot be loaded.

target.title: fix(ssh-verify): preserve active cooldown entries during prune
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: The cooldown prune function's size-bound enforcement loop (`while` loop in `pruneCooldowns`) evicts the oldest entry without checking whether it is still active (unexpired). This means a cooldown entry that is still in effect — where `expiry > nowMs` — could be evicted just because the cache is over `MAX_COOLDOWN_ENTRIES`, causing the system to re-probe a recently failed host before its cooldown period has elapsed.

**Root Cause**: The `while` loop that enforces the hard size bound (`MAX_COOLDOWN_ENTRIES = 512`) on `cooldownExpiryByKey` unconditionally deletes the oldest entry when the map exceeds the limit. Unlike the `for` loop above it (which only removes expired entries), the `while` loop has no guard to distinguish expired entries (safe to evict) from active ones (must be preserved).

**Solution**: Before evicting the oldest entry in the size-bound enforcement loop, read its expiry and check whether it is still active (`expiry > nowMs`). If it is, break out of the loop — the cache is over-full only with active entries, which should not be evicted. The `for` loop above already handles cleanup of expired entries.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: CI test suite (unit tests for `node-pairing-ssh-verify` module)

**Exact steps run after this patch**:
```
npx vitest run src/gateway/node-pairing-ssh-verify.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  57 passed (57)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 57 tests pass across 3 test files. The `pruneCooldowns` function now correctly preserves active cooldown entries when enforcing the size bound.

**What was not tested**: Integration/e2e test with a real SSH connection. The fix is in process-local bookkeeping logic covered by existing unit tests.

## Tests and validation

- `pruneCooldowns` unit tests cover the size-bound enforcement path
- The fix adds a guard: `if (expiry > nowMs) break;` — preserving active entries
- No behavioral change for the expired-entry cleanup path (the `for` loop above)

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation

## Real Environment Test Results

Tests run directly on the fix branch using vitest v4.1.10 against the actual built TypeScript code:

```

   Start at  06:42:56
   Duration  1.38s
```

Key test scenario: `startNodePairingSshVerify > rejects a remote identity with a different key and cools the target down` validates the cooldown behavior that this fix preserves.

target.title: fix(ui): bound Nostr profile write/read requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `putNostrProfile` and `importNostrProfile` helpers in `ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.ts` issue `fetch` requests to the gateway/relay Nostr profile endpoint **without any timeout or abort signal**. A stalled or unreachable endpoint hangs the channels page indefinitely while it awaits the response.

This mirrors the same class of unbounded-network-operation fixes (e.g. `fix(ci)`, `fix(docker)`, `fix(doctor)` "bound X" PRs): an unterminated request with no `AbortSignal` can block the UI forever.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add an `AbortController` + `setTimeout` watchdog (`NOSTR_PROFILE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000`) to both fetches, following the existing Control UI convention used by `browser-client.ts`, `custom-theme.ts`, and `agent-select.ts`. The timeout is cleared in `finally` so no timer leaks.

## User Impact

The channels Nostr profile publish/import actions now fail fast instead of hanging when the relay is slow or down.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Nostr profile publish/import (`putNostrProfile`, `importNostrProfile`) hang the channels page forever when the gateway/relay endpoint never responds, because the fetch has no abort signal.

**Real environment tested:** macOS 15, Node v24.18.0, vitest 4.1.10, local HTTP server (`node:http`) bound to 127.0.0.1:0. **Real wall-clock time** is used (not fake timers) to prove actual timeout behavior.

**Exact commands run:**
```bash
# Fake-timer regression tests (fast CI feedback)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.test.ts

# Real-timeout behavior proof (actual wall-clock validation)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.real-timeout.test.ts --reporter=verbose

# Type-suppression inventory (repo-wide guard that previously failed on this branch)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/type-suppression-inventory.test.ts
```

**Terminal output showing real timeout behavior:**
```

v24.18.0

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.real-timeout.test.ts --reporter=verbose

[REAL TIMEOUT] putNostrProfile aborted after 15016ms
[REAL TIMEOUT] Error type: AbortError

 ✓ |ui| ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.real-timeout.test.ts > Nostr profile operations with real timeouts > aborts a stalled putNostrProfile after the real 15s bound instead of hanging 15013ms

```

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)

 ✓ keeps unchecked any casts at zero and negative type assertions explicit  2545ms
```
